description: We are a multidisciplinary team of developers and designers building a farmer-centered web tool for the Field Shift challenge. Our mission is to translate complex NASA Earth observations into intuitive, actionable insights. We aim to help agricultural communities optimize crop rotations, conserve water, and build climate resilience. We are excited to collaborate, innovate, and develop sustainable, data-driven solutions to support global agriculture.
summary:
Choclito is an offline-first mobile application designed to empower smallholder farmers in regions with limited internet connectivity, directly addressing the NASA "Field Shift" challenge. Built with React Native and Expo Router, Choclito translates complex Earth observation datasets into actionable, localized agricultural insights.

The app allows farmers to record crop status, report local anomalies (e.g., droughts, frosts), and receive predictive planting calendars and climate alerts without relying on a constant network connection. By bridging the gap between high-level satellite data and on-the-ground farming decisions, Choclito mitigates risks posed by phenomena like El Niño. It is a critical tool for optimizing water usage in drought-prone areas and fostering community-driven climate resilience through decentralized data.
details:
What it does & How it works Choclito is an offline-capable mobile application that provides smallholder farmers with hyper-localized climate forecasts, optimal planting windows, and community-driven alerts. Operating on an offline-first architecture, the app allows users to log crop conditions and local anomalies (like lack of water or frost) even without a cell signal. Once connectivity is restored, the app syncs this crowdsourced ground-truth data with the cloud, updating the community map.

Benefits & Intended Impact The core benefit is democratizing complex scientific data. Instead of showing raw precipitation metrics, Choclito translates NASA data into actionable advice like "Water tomorrow morning; soil moisture is at 12%." The intended impact is to protect crops from extreme weather events, optimize scarce water resources (crucial during El Niño years), and build a collaborative network where farmers act as in-situ sensors for their region.
